source_text: Christi caro, quia de Maria natus est, cuius virginis caro sicut ceterorum omnium ex Adam fuerat propagata, nihil distet a carne peccati, et sine ulla distinctione Apostolus dixisse credatur, eum fuisse missum in similitudine carnis peccati ut nulla sit caro peccati, ne hoc sit et Christi hanc apostolicam sententiam me non intellexisse
pass_a_gloss: Of-Christ flesh, because about/from Mary born is, whose of-the-virgin flesh as ceterorum of-all from Adam fuerat propagata, nothing distet from in-flesh of-sin, and without ulla distinctione apostle dixisse credatur, him to-have-been missum in similitudine of-flesh of-sin so-that/as no may-be flesh of-sin, lest this may-be and of-Christ this apostolicam position me not intellexisse.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian argued that Christ’s flesh, born from Mary whose flesh descended from Adam like everyone else’s, cannot be distinguished from other human flesh in the interpretation of ‘the likeness of sinful flesh’ (Romans 8:3). Julian’s conclusion, as Augustine restates it, is that no flesh is sinful, so that Christ’s flesh will not be sinful either.
You have not understood this apostolic statement.
